transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
President Trump is spending the Thanksgiving holiday at his club in Palm Beach
where he signed a disaster declaration for Florida following days of relentless rain.
It's been raining continuously. It's the craziest thing.
It's stopped now, very unusual for Florida, but it's record-setting rains in a lot of areas in Florida.
We're beating up pretty badly, and we're releasing funding, immediate funding.
Parts of Florida's east coast has been deluged with rainfall this month,
and Florida's St. John's River rose to record levels.
Meanwhile, that Thanksgiving storm has knocked out power to hundreds of thousands of homes and businesses
on the east coast and coastal flooding has affected areas from North Carolina to New York.
California has also faced coastal flooding, and Missouri and Illinois got socked by heavy snow.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is preparing Ukrainians for a new mass strike in his nightly address Thursday.
Zelensky said Ukraine has information that Russia is planning a new strike in the coming days.
His warning is the second he issued this week.
China, Japan, and countries in the European Union are among those protesting
the latest U.S. tariffs being proposed by the Trump administration.
The White House frames the new levies as it responds to unfair trade practices.
Jan Kamisen Brumby reports that Singapore also pushing back on claims
that American firms are being disadvantaged by an overproduction of cheaper factory goods overseas.
Singapore's Ministry of Energy Trade and Industry says it disagrees with the findings
and is "very disappointed" with Washington's proposal.
The unusually strongly worded statement comes after the U.S. proposed new tariffs, citing unfair trading practices.
Singapore says the tariffs do not consider the structure of the city-state's economy,
adding that the island's free trade agreements are aligned with world trade organization rules.
Elsewhere, local media reports that Malaysia is continuing talks with the United States to keep proposed tariffs below 19%.
Vietnam, meanwhile, says it will work with the United States to complete a trade deal.
I'm Jan Kamisen Brumby in Taipei.
Federal spending on water conservation in the Colorado River basin went down by more than 70%
in the first year and a half of the Trump administration.
From Member Station KJZZ, Alex Hager reports on the study from an independent research group.
The report from Prospect Partners found hundreds of millions of dollars were cut for programs around the arid west.
In many cases, the federal government broke existing contracts that paid for water conservation.
Bernie Kluger is the report's author. He advised the Secretary of Agriculture during the Biden administration.
We have never seen anything on this scale in the nation's history.
We're literally tens of thousands of contracts with farmers, ranchers, and small business owners were canceled, and the money was clawed back.
The funding cutbacks have hit farms, businesses, tribes, and cities from Wyoming to Southern California.
For NPR News, I'm Alex Hager in Phoenix.
This is NPR News. The future of a federal law that requires employers to provide reasonable accommodations for pregnancy and pregnancy-related conditions is in question.
NPR's Andrea Shue reports on the multiple challenges faced by the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act.
This month, the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals struck down the law on a technicality.
The court found not enough house lawmakers were present in the chamber when they passed the measure as part of a larger package in late 2022.
Under COVID-era rules, many members voted from home.
For now, the ruling only applies to the plaintiff in the case, the state of Texas. Private employers must still comply with the law.
Meanwhile, the Trump administration is seeking to narrow the types of conditions covered by the law.
A proposed rule is expected soon. Under current rules, employers have to provide reasonable accommodations for not just pregnancy and childbirth,
but also menopause and fertility-related conditions and others.
Andrea Shue, NPR News.
Authorities in New Mexico were on the lookout for a pregnant inmate who escaped by stealing a corrections transport vehicle.
The state corrections department says three officers who accompanied 26-year-old Rebecca Taylor were stopped at a restaurant Wednesday when she climbed into the driver's seat and drove away.
Officials say she was unrestrained due to her pregnancy.
Asian chairs are advancing in Friday trading, South Korea's benchmark up 4% and Japan's Nikkei share average has gained 1.9% ahead of Wall Street's reopening following the Thanksgiving holiday.
I'm Giles Snyder, NPR News.
This message comes from Rosetta Stone, offering an alternative approach to language learning.
Moving past rote memorization, the app guides users to intuitively think in a second language using images and contextual audio, mimicking how people acquire speech as children.
The platform also includes advanced speech recognition technology that compares a learner's pronunciation directly with native speakers to refine accent precision.
Learn more about their new Rosetta Stone Sapphire app at RosettaStone.com.
